Item 3.02 Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities

On September 26, 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (the “Company”) entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) to acquire all of the equity interests in World Labs Technologies, Inc. (“World Labs”) (the “Acquisition”) for a total purchase price of approximately $8.2 billion to be paid in shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.01 per share (“Common Stock”), to stockholders of World Labs, subject to customary adjustments. At this time, the number of shares to be issued in connection with the Acquisition is not known and will be calculated based on the daily volume-weighted average price of a share of Common Stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market over the ten (10) consecutive trading-day period ending on and including the second trading day immediately preceding the closing date of the Acquisition.

The Company intends to issue the shares of Common Stock in reliance upon the exemptions from registration afforded by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and/or Rule 506 of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act. The issuance is not being conducted in connection with a public offering, and no public solicitation or advertisement will be made or relied upon in connection with the issuance of the shares.

Item 2.02 Results of Operations and Financial Condition.
On August 4, 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. ("AMD") announced its financial results for its second quarter of 2026 ended June 27, 2026 in a press release that is attached hereto as Exhibit 99.1. Attached hereto as Exhibit 99.2 is a presentation regarding AMD's second quarter of 2026.

The attached Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2, in addition to financial results presented on a U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (“GAAP”) basis, contains certain non-GAAP financial information and forward-looking financial guidance. Certain of these non-GAAP financial measures will be used in AMD’s earnings conference call. A reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to their nearest GAAP equivalents is provided in the data tables at the end of the attached Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. These non-GAAP financial measures should be viewed in addition to and not as a substitute for or superior to AMD’s reported results prepared in accordance with GAAP.

The information in this report furnished pursuant to Items 2.02 and 7.01, including Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 attached hereto, shall not be deemed “filed” for the purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), or otherwise subject to the liabilities of that section. It may only be incorporated by reference in another filing under the Exchange Act or the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, if such subsequent filing specifically references the information furnished pursuant to Items 2.02 and 7.01 of this report.

runs.summary: AMD’s reported growth is led by Data Center, while performance across other segments is uneven and recent results leave current-quarter trends unresolved. A confirmed earnings report and a newly announced deployment partnership provide near-term catalysts, with their financial effects still uncertain. The valuation screen is elevated relative to a narrow peer set, and execution, cyclicality, and acquisition risks remain relevant.

keyFindings.text: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, revenue grew +44.1% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) and gross profit grew +71.0% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year. Operating income grew +415.8% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27), amplified by a low prior-year base.

Data Center was the main growth engine: first-half segment revenue grew 81% year over year, driven mainly by EPYC processors and Instinct MI350 Series GPUs. Second-quarter segment operating margin was 31.3%, compared with -4.8% a year earlier; the comparison partly reflects prior-year MI308 export-control charges.
First-half segment performance was uneven. Client and Gaming revenue grew 13%, while its operating margin was 15.5%; Embedded segment operating margin was 39.1%.

For the six months ended June 27, operating cash flow from continuing operations grew +121.6% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year, while reported capex outflow grew +142.3% YoY (6-month period ending 2026-06-27). The continuing-operations cash-flow-less-capex proxy was positive, but does not establish returns on investment.

Yahoo provider trailing EPS is $3.92, with accounting scope and period basis undisclosed. SEC approximate diluted EPS TTM through June 27, 2026 was $3.90 for total operations and $3.92 for continuing operations; both SEC values add per-share periods without reweighting diluted shares.

risks.text: The latest issuer financial results end June 27, 2026, while the analysis date is October 28; current-quarter revenue, margins, shipments, and cash generation remain unreported in supplied issuer evidence.

AMD identifies rapid competition, semiconductor cyclicality, dependence on customer-market conditions, product-launch execution, and possible loss of a significant customer as risks. The supplied filing excerpts do not quantify current customer concentration.
The supplied peer comparison uses four usable peers, only one classified as core, excludes Nvidia under the screen’s market-cap rule, and mixes quote and balance-sheet dates.
The World Labs agreement’s closing status, final share issuance, integration costs, and operating contribution remain unresolved in the supplied evidence.

catalysts.text: AMD is scheduled to report fiscal Q3 2026 results on November 3 after market close, an issuer-confirmed date. The report can update operating evidence beyond June; supplied estimates are provider estimates, not company guidance.
Further detail on Data Center margins, accelerator shipments, Helios deployment scale, and utilization would clarify whether reported demand translates into profitable deliveries.
Further World Labs disclosures could clarify transaction completion, share issuance, integration costs, and operating contribution.

runs.summary: AMD’s operating evidence shows rapid growth led by Data Center, alongside uneven segment performance and higher capital spending. The next major update is the issuer-confirmed third-quarter report. Valuation comparisons and recent price behavior provide context, while limited peer coverage, unresolved acquisition details, and the gap in reported results leave key uncertainties.

keyFindings.text: For the six months ended June 27, 2026, revenue grew 44.1% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year, and gross profit grew 71.0% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27). Operating income grew 415.8% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27), amplified by a low prior-year base.

Data Center segment revenue grew 81% year over year in the first half, primarily on demand for EPYC processors and Instinct MI350 Series GPUs. Second-quarter segment operating margin was 31.3% (3-month period ending 2026-06-27), compared with -4.8% in the year-earlier quarter; the comparison partly reflects the absence of prior-year MI308 export-control charges.

First-half segment performance was uneven: Client and Gaming revenue grew 13%, while its operating margin declined to 15.5% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) from 19.2%. Embedded revenue was $1.9B and its operating margin was 39.1% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27).

For the six months ended June 27, operating cash flow from continuing operations grew 121.6% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27) year over year; capital expenditure grew 142.3% (6-month period ending 2026-06-27). The continuing-operations cash-flow-less-capex proxy was $4.1B (6-month period ending 2026-06-27); it does not establish returns on investment.

Yahoo reports provider trailing EPS of $3.92, with accounting scope and period basis undisclosed. SEC approximate TTM diluted EPS through June 27, 2026 was $3.90 for total operations and $3.92 for continuing operations. The SEC figures add per-share periods without reweighting diluted shares.

The peer valuation comparison has four usable peers, one classified as core, and excludes Nvidia under the screen’s market-cap rule; the resulting comparison has a narrow basis.
